subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw add a public memorySearch exclusion/path-hygiene contract now, and should that contract be builtin-only first or cover builtin, QMD, status diagnostics, and index identity together?
rationale: The request changes public memorySearch configuration and recall-corpus semantics, and repository policy treats config/default additions and memory/session state as compatibility-sensitive rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
options.body: Land the open exclusion PR or a successor after fixing merge semantics, index identity, and explicit builtin-only docs while tracking QMD and broader diagnostics separately.

options.title: Require cross-backend contract
options.body: Pause exclusion work until builtin indexing, QMD collections, watcher behavior, stale-index cleanup, docs, and diagnostics share one accepted exclusion model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer a public exclusion config and focus on clearer path-drift, broad-extraPaths, benchmark-contamination guidance, and status warnings.

recommendation.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
recommendation.body: Land the open exclusion PR or a successor after fixing merge semantics, index identity, and explicit builtin-only docs while tracking QMD and broader diagnostics separately.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans memory-host implementation, docs, config policy, and path-hygiene product scope where steipete has the strongest recent current-main history signal.
